first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both deteriorating, and the archived evidence points to shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction as durable drivers of early adoption. I would verify those records before committing, while also checking the promotional-pricing evidence because competitor pricing is an important alternative. A small guarded test focused on qualified activation and downstream conversion can address the immediate funnel decline without committing to potentially margin-eroding discounts. Success should require improvement in activation and time-to-value without deterioration in qualified pipeline, retention, or revenue quality.

final.rationale: Run a standard, segmented onboarding-simplification experiment, prioritizing the current declines in completion and activation. Shortened onboarding has confirmed gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, making it the strongest sustainable-growth response. Apply signup-field reduction only to SMBs, where evidence holds, and monitor qualified revenue and retention because the prior signup test slightly reduced retention. Do not use promotional pricing: the verified discount cohort lost 12% of 30-day retention and failed to survive renewal. Judge success on activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue rather than top-of-funnel conversion alone.
